A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SelvaBox dataset and benchmarking work. Their main text, tables, figures, algorithms, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original detector benchmarks, resolution and spatial-extent experiments, multi-resolution training results, and cross-dataset evaluations, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds trained-baseline comparisons, resolution-transfer tests, RF1 threshold analyses, and statistical comparisons of crown-size distributions.

M1.justification: The detector architectures, crop-and-resize multi-resolution procedure, raster aggregation, and greedy RF1 computation remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix D.1 retain the same procedures. Additional baseline training and annotation documentation do not introduce a new proposed detector.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SelvaBox rasters and the same five external benchmark datasets, and retain ReforesTree qualitative examples. The additional experiments vary model training and evaluation within existing datasets and resolution levels; they introduce no additional geographic, biome, or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Tables 4–5 expand the corresponding six-row comparisons in v1 Tables 5–6 to fourteen rows. Faster R-CNN joins these cross-dataset comparisons, DeepForest gains SelvaBox-only and multi-dataset trained variants, and a NeonTreeEvaluation-only DINO control is added. The released Detectree2 and DeepForest comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds architecture-by-training-dataset controls with specified training budgets, evaluates fixed-resolution models at other resolutions, and sweeps RF1 matching IoU from 0.50 to 0.95 with independently tuned NMS. It also revises the annotation account from six biologists and usually single-pass annotation to five experts and systematic review. This establishes a reported protocol revision, not when or whether the released annotations were changed.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing resolution ablations and qualitative examples, v2 adds cross-resolution failure analyses in Figures 3 and 8, RF1 threshold sensitivity on four datasets in Figure 4 and Appendix E, and quantitative crown-size distribution comparisons in Appendix F.2. These test robustness and dataset distinctiveness that v1 did not analyze this way.

E5.justification: V1 already reports standard deviations and references multiple seeds without specifying their number. V2 Tables 4–5 explicitly identify three seeds for trained models and single released checkpoints for external models. Appendix F.2 additionally introduces two-sample KS tests, statistics, and p-values. The seed disclosure does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: The original resolution tables, Table 18, and retained benchmark scores are unchanged. V2 adds extensive results for additional training conditions: for example, SelvaBox-trained DeepForest and Faster R-CNN obtain SelvaBox RF1_75 scores of 38.00 and 36.37. It also adds cross-resolution curves, RF1 threshold curves, and distribution statistics in Table 20. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix F.2 adds the approximate KS p-value relationship p ≈ 2 exp(-2nD²) and a sample-size-based argument for extremely small p-values. This is a limited mathematical addition. The RF1 definition, aggregation equations, and matching algorithms remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introductory contributions retain their scientific scope. The conclusion now describes the annotations as expert-verified, replacing v1's explicit qualification that they usually lacked secondary review, and omits the explicit second-largest-overall dataset claim. The central dataset, performance, and generalization claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations for photo-based validation, interpretations of RF1 threshold behavior and crown-size differences, and practical model-selection boundaries in Section 5.4. It replaces the single-pass annotation limitation with systematic-review claims and residual-noise cautions. The conflicting annotation histories are not reconciled, so improved underlying annotation quality is not established.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.3 documents annotator preparation, systematic 60 × 60 m grid review, correction, and consensus procedures; Section 3 discloses DSM assistance. Tables 11 and 15 add training and inference settings for the expanded comparisons. The reproducibility statement adds access guidance for raster-level annotations and smaller model variants, while existing hardware and preprocessing details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces v1's assertion that previous research had not evaluated aggregated raster-level predictions with acknowledgment of OAM-TCD's raster-level keypoint recall, positioning RF1 as a detection-based extension. Background references are pruned and relevant satellite, annotation, and statistical sources are added, including Laliberté et al. (2025) and Marsaglia et al. (2003). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The introduction, related-work discussion, benchmarking explanations, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting and condensation. V2 separates ethical considerations from the conclusion, adds practical advice and a reproducibility statement, reorganizes the appendices, and includes an LLM-use disclosure. These changes substantially revise the narrative beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: V2 expands and groups the main comparison tables, adds relative-gain columns, four RF1 threshold plots, and Table 20. Resolution figures gain cross-resolution curves, and the cross-dataset crown-size histogram becomes a finer-binned line plot. The orthomosaic table moves to the appendix, and conference formatting changes headers, typography, caption placement, and layout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical case through architecture comparisons using common training datasets, direct resolution-transfer tests, and RF1 threshold analyses. These reduce important gaps in v1's evidence about model versus training-data effects and robustness; expanded protocol and seed disclosures also improve reproducibility. The annotation-review history remains unreconciled, and the validation source for BCI50ha's new threshold sweeps is unclear, but these limitations do not outweigh the stronger comparative evidence.
